newsitem.title: USA: Coke Ent launches bold North American bid.
newsitem.headline: Coke Ent launches bold North American bid.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc., the largest of the Coke bottlers, is embarking on a bold new plan to consolidate the United States and Canada into a single market for Coke-brand soft drinks, analysts said on Tuesday.

While it may be 12 to 18 months before the Atlanta-based company has acquired and restructured Coca-Cola Beverages Ltd of Canada and Coca-Cola Bottling Co of New York Inc, higher margins and bigger market shares are sure to result from the $1.66 billion overall transaction.
"It's going to take a while for them to get their act together," said Roy Burry, an analyst at Oppenheimer & Co.

"They have to make the necessary restructuring moves to integrate the U.S. and Canadian businesses ... We're talking one to two years there. I would guess that subsequent to that time, you would begin to see an increase in per capita consumption."
Coca-Cola Enterprises announced its plans to buy the two companies earlier on Tuesday.

The transaction, expected to be completed by the end of September, would immediately boost Coke Enterprises' annual revenues by about 15 percent and give the huge bottler ready access to two new markets containing 51 million consumers.

The company said an immediate effect for investors on Wall Street would be flat profit growth in 1997, following last year's 38 percent improvement in earnings per share. But Coke Enterprises said growth would quickly begin to return in 1998.
"We expect earnings to be flat this year. And then in 1998, we expect to produce a 15-20 percent earnings per share growth rate," company spokeswoman Laura Asman said.
Coca-Cola Co has a 45 percent stake in Coke Enterprises, one of its nine so-called anchor bottlers worldwide.

With the addition of the two new bottlers, Coke Enterprises would control 65 percent of Coca-Cola's North American can and bottle volume by adding to markets that currently span the U.S. South, the Midwest, the Pacific Northwest and California.

Coke Canada represents 95 percent of Coke brand sales in the country, while Coke New York would add New York City and New Jersey plus Connecticut, Massachusetts, Vermont and New Hampshire. New markets would make for new clashes with rival PepsiCo Inc in some tough Pepsi-Cola markets, and with Canadian beverage company Cott Corp.
Analysts were not sure how successful Coke Enterprises would be in raising per capital consumption in Canada.

Coke Enterprises said its strategy would be to restructure the two operations to bring them into accordance with its own decentralized system and then to support the operations from contiguous existing markets.

A general aim would be to move the two new markets towards an average U.S. per capita consumption rate of 320 eight-ounce servings of Coke brand products a year. Canada currently stands at a consumption rate of 228 servings and New York at 214, according to Coke Enterprises.
"There's room to expand the business (in Canada) but I wouldn't be willing to say they could get it to the level that's been reached here," said George Thompson, an analyst at Prudential Securities.

"Cola wars are a figment of the media's imagination. These are very rationally run businesses. Sure, if they take share there'll be a whole lot of publicity, probably. But what's important is that they do it on a profitable basis, and that's highly likely to be the case," Thompson said.
